intended_object: This is the Eilenberg-swindle isomorphism V ⊕ R^(ℕ) ≅ R^(ℕ), built from a chosen splitting R^(ℕ) ≅ V ⊕ W. The docstring ("every chosen direct summand of `ℕ →₀ R` is absorbed by `ℕ →₀ R`") and the module doc ("packages a countable Eilenberg swindle") say so.
explanation:
The definition is not a mathematical notion such as a structure, invariant or operation. It is a particular linear equivalence that witnesses a lemma: the free module of countable rank absorbs any of its direct summands. It is defined as the general file-local construction `prodEquivOfCountableSelfSum`, applied with M = ℕ →₀ R and the self-sum equivalence `natFinsuppCountableSelfSum`. Its only use in the file is as an intermediate step in building `rightIdealProdEndNatFinsuppEquiv`, which concerns complemented right ideals of End(R^(ℕ)). So it is an auxiliary construction inside a proof (an instance of the Eilenberg swindle), not a definition of a mathematical object.

Read as a statement, it is correct. The construction composes standard equivalences: V × M ≅ V × (ℕ →₀ M) ≅ V × (ℕ →₀ V) × (ℕ →₀ W) ≅ (ℕ →₀ V) × (ℕ →₀ W) ≅ ℕ →₀ M ≅ M. Specialising to ℕ →₀ R is deliberate, because the general version already exists as `prodEquivOfCountableSelfSum`. Mathlib has no dedicated declaration for this swindle isomorphism.
